messages.subject: lavaan vs blavaan
parts:
Hi!
I wonder what to make of a SEM model that as a non-significant P-value for Chi-square under DWLS but a significant P-value under Robust. I know that the data quality is not the best, so I tried also the Bayesian version. But there, I do not get a test-statistic for too many missing data, however good convergence. 
See the outputs:

> summary(fit_SEM_BN_POFall, standardized = TRUE,

+         fit.measures = TRUE, rsquare = TRUE)

lavaan (0.5-23.1097) converged normally after  59 iterations

 

                                                  Used       Total

  Number of observations                           111         144

 

  Estimator                                       DWLS      Robust

  Minimum Function Test Statistic              109.714     192.865

  Degrees of freedom                               144         144

  P-value (Chi-square)                           0.985       0.004

  Scaling correction factor                                  1.017

  Shift parameter                                           84.984

    for simple second-order correction (Mplus variant)


> summary(fitBSEM_BN_POFall)

blavaan (0.2-4) results of 9811 samples after 25000 adapt+burnin iterations

 

                                                  Used       Total

  Number of observations                           111         144

 

  Statistic                              

  Value                                  


Can I use the Bayesian parameter estimates and use the test-statistics from the frequentist analysis? Or is the data quality such that I should not use the SEM at all? 


Thanks for a quick reply. Best wishes from Norway,

Ulrich

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: lavaan vs blavaan
parts: I wonder what to make of a SEM model that as a non-significant P-value for Chi-square under DWLS but a significant P-value under Robust.

It's usually the other way around, since the robust correction is meant to correct for Type I error inflation (at least with continuous data, for which it was originally intended to be used).  But that is the average behavior over many samples.  You just have one sample, so you can't draw an inference about why this happened to happen. 

The uncorrected test statistic is only provided for the sake of completion (and because it is used in the robust chi-squared difference test).  You should pay attention only to the robust column because that is the one expected to behave better on average across many samples.  However, you have a very small sample, and past research has shown that even this robust test statistic has inflated error rates until sample sizes are very large, especially when categories are asymmetric.

http://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/10705511.2014.859510
I tried also the Bayesian version. But there, I do not get a test-statistic for too many missing data

Huh?  If you are looking for the chi-squared (derived from the minimum fit function using DWLS) in blavaan output, you won't find it with complete data because it is not a Bayesian statistic.  There is a PPP value, and some information criteria available for model comparison.
Can I use the Bayesian parameter estimates and use the test-statistics from the frequentist analysis? Or is the data quality such that I should not use the SEM at all?

No, your test statistic is derived from the estimator, so you need to report one set of results or the other.  Again, you might be looking for something that isn't there in blavaan.  Perhaps this article will shed some light.

http://dx.doi.org/10.1037/a0026802

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Postdoctoral Researcher, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
UvA web page: http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen

messages.author: 82889e926eb5165e
messages.subject: Re: lavaan vs blavaan
parts:
Ulrich

test is an argument for the blavaan functions, it means that when you ran the model in blavaan that argument is set to "none", what this do is to not estimate any fit measure. This is only recommended for time, it runs faster without it.

simply run the model without setting test="none", that way you will have the ppp, and ICs

bye

Hi Mauricio,

thanks for your post. I have not included the test="none" argument. But I do have two "ordered" dummy variables (group and enquiry) in the regressions. Might this be the problem?
The variables competence and autonomy are correlated (VIF=2,6) - and I have those latent constructs parceled to reduce complexity, and I have now run a reduced model in lavaan with OK fit. 
The same model in blavaan does converge pretty  fast, but does not give me the ppp.

Here's the model:

VModel3_Var <- '
# measurement model
competence =~ help + structure
#autonomy =~ choice + reason + respect 

#RS =~RS_1 + RS_2 + RS_3 +RS_4
RT =~RT_1 + RT_2 + RT_3 + RT_4
PO =~ PO_1 + PO_2 + PO_3 + PO_4 + PO_5

# regressions
competence ~ PO + Group + enquiry
#autonomy ~ PO + Group + enquiry  
#RS ~PO + Group + enquiry
RT ~PO + Group + enquiry
PO ~Group + enquiry'

The blavaan command is:
fitBSEM_Fall <- bsem(VModel3_Var, data = subset(HD_SEM_BN, 
                                         enquiry == c("1", "2")),
                                ordered= c("Group", "enquiry"),
                          dp = dpriors(nu = "dnorm(0,1e-3)", 
                                       alpha = "dnorm(0,1e-2)",
                                       lambda = "dnorm(0,1e-2)",
                                       beta = "dnorm(0,1e-2)",
                                       itheta = "dgamma(1,.5)",
                                       ipsi = "dgamma(1,.5)",
                                       rho = "dbeta(1,1)",
                                       ibpsi = "dwish(iden,3)"),
                          cp = "srs",
                          convergence = "auto")

summary(fitBSEM_Fall)

What do I do wrong? 
Thanks! 
Ulrich

messages.author: 82889e926eb5165e
messages.subject: Re: lavaan vs blavaan
parts:
Ulrich

It may be the ordered argument, as far as I understand, blavaan still doesnt handle categorical variables. It may be estimating the model, but not calculating any fit measure, since the fit measures are in function of the log-likelihood with continuous variables. 

Would recommend to try without the ordered argument, if they are dummy code, the model should run fine, I know is not ideal to treat a dummy this way.

If the problem persist, you could post in the blavaan forum, so the developer can take a look at it
https://groups.google.com/forum/?fromgroups#!forum/blavaan

bye
